::::{#exm-truncated-power-spline}
#### A cubic spline with one knot

Take $d = 3$, one knot at $\xi = 2$, and

$$s(x) = 1 + x + 0.5 (x - 2)_+^3.$$

By @thm-truncated-power-spline, $s$ is a cubic spline.
The table gives each derivative of the truncated term $0.5(x - 2)_+^3$
on each side of the knot,
using $0.5\, h^{(j)}(x) = 0.5 \cdot \frac{3!}{(3-j)!}(x - 2)^{3-j}$ for $x > 2$,
where $h(x) = (x - 2)_+^3$ as in @thm-truncated-power-spline:

| Derivative order $j$ | Left of $\xi = 2$ | Right of $\xi = 2$ | Limit at $\xi$ from the right |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | $0.5(x - 2)^3$ | 0 |
| 1 | 0 | $1.5(x - 2)^2$ | 0 |
| 2 | 0 | $3(x - 2)$ | 0 |
| 3 | 0 | $3$ | 3 |

The function and its first two derivatives agree on both sides of the knot,
but the third derivative jumps by $0.5 \cdot 3! = 3$.
At $x = 3$:

$$
\ba
s(3) &= 1 + 3 + 0.5 (3 - 2)_+^3
&& \text{(substitute } x = 3\text{)}
\\ &= 1 + 3 + 0.5 \cdot 1
&& \text{(} (1)_+^3 = 1\text{)}
\\ &= 4.5
&& \text{(add)}
\ea
$$

whereas at $x = 1$ the truncated term is 0 and $s(1) = 2$.
::::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::::{#exm-truncated-power-not-spline}
#### A lower-degree truncated term breaks smoothness (counterexample)

Replacing the truncated cubic in @exm-truncated-power-spline
with a truncated square gives

$$u(x) = 1 + x + 0.5 (x - 2)_+^2.$$

The function $u$ is piecewise cubic (each piece has degree at most 3),
but it is not a cubic spline.
Its second derivative is 0 to the left of $\xi = 2$
and $0.5 \cdot 2 = 1$ to the right of $\xi = 2$,
so the second derivative jumps at the knot,
violating the continuity of derivatives through order $d - 1 = 2$
required by @def-spline.
::::
